STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.claim: God's enduring reality offsets the dualities: verses 26–27 stress that God remains while everything else passes away.
STUDYQURAN:55:intro/r11.anchor: vv. 26–27, which emphasize that God remains while all else fades away

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.claim: Only God is immortal; all other beings perish.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r2.anchor: God alone is immortal and all the rest are mortal.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.claim: The created order, provision, divine wisdom, sovereignty, and harmony entail that all creation will end and only God remain; all will be judged without being able to challenge His decisions or intercede without permission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p120/r4.anchor: Only the exalted and revered person of God will remain. Everyone will be gathered before Him one day and He will deal with everyone in the manner that person is worthy of.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r2.claim: The collective expression all who are on it uses a masculine pronoun because rational beings predominate; the pronoun refers back to the earth mentioned earlier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r2.anchor: وعبر بمن في قوله: كل من عليها تغليبا لمن يعقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.claim: Perishing means the extinction of every created thing, while face denotes a thing's reality; God is exempt from bodily limbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p61#2/r3.anchor: والفناء عبارة عن إعدام جميع الموجودات من حيوان وغيره، والوجه يعبر به عن حقيقة الشيء

NAHHAS:v4p308/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p308/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p308/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the earth God spread out: everyone on earth perishes.
NAHHAS:v4p308/r1.anchor: الضمير يعود على الأرض وضعها أي كل من على الأرض يفنى ويهلك

NAHHAS:v4p308/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p308/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p308/r2.claim: The original form has ياء; its vowel was made still because it was heavy, then it was deleted before the still tanwin.
NAHHAS:v4p308/r2.anchor: والأصل فإني استثقلت الحركة في الياء فسكنت ثم حذفت لسكونها وسكون التنوين بعدها

SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r1.claim: The masculine rational form من includes all beings on earth, rational and non-rational alike.
SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r1.anchor: غلب من يعقل على غيره، وجميعهم مراد

SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r2.claim: The pronoun عليها refers to the earth.

SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:26/r3.claim: Some say earth need not have been mentioned earlier, comparing 38:32; critics answer that 55:10 already names it.

ZAJJAJ:v5p99/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p99/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p99/r1.claim: “Whoever is upon it” means whoever is on the earth.
ZAJJAJ:v5p99/r1.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: (كل من عليها فان (26) معناه على الأرض.

ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r2.claim: All living beings on earth and in the heavens will pass away.
ASAD-NOTES:55:24/r2.anchor: All that lives on earth or in the heavens [10] is bound to pass away

ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n10/r1.claim: The phrase literally means everyone who is upon it, referring to earth.

ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n10/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n10/r2.speaker: Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n10/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir includes the heavens, since the pronoun apparently relates to the whole universe.
ASAD-NOTES:55:24#n10/r2.anchor: according to Ibn Kathir, in the heavens - since the pronoun

NASHR:v1p224#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p224#2/r1.claim: Because a reader cannot recite a whole sūra or story in one breath, pauses and corresponding resumptions are necessary; they must preserve meaning and comprehension.
NASHR:v1p224#2/r1.anchor: وجب حينئذ اختيار وقف للتنفس والاستراحة وتعين ارتضاء ابتداء بعد التنفس والاستراحة

NASHR:v1p224#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
NASHR:v1p224#2/r2.claim: ʿAlī defines tartīl as knowing the stopping places and giving letters their proper articulation; Ibn al-Jazarī says this proves knowledge of stopping is obligatory.
NASHR:v1p224#2/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب - رضي الله عنه - قوله: الترتيل معرفة الوقوف وتجويد الحروف

NASHR:v1p224#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
NASHR:v1p224#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says Companions learned faith before Qurʾān and each sūra's lawful and forbidden matters, commands, prohibitions, and stopping places; the author treats this as proof of Companion consensus.
NASHR:v1p224#2/r3.anchor: وروينا عن ابن عمر - رضي الله عنهما - أنه قال: قد عشنا برهة من دهرنا

NASHR:v1p224#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p224#2/r4.claim: The author says attention to stopping was transmitted from the early community, naming Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Yaʿqūb, and ʿĀṣim among its authorities.
NASHR:v1p224#2/r4.anchor: وصح، بل تواتر عندنا تعلمه والاعتناء به من السلف الصالح كأبي جعفر

NASHR:v1p224#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p224#2/r5.claim: Many later authorities made knowledge of stopping and resuming a condition for granting reading authorization; teachers marked every letter's stopping place with their fingers.
NASHR:v1p224#2/r5.anchor: ومن ثم اشترط كثير من أئمة الخلف على المجيز أن لا يجيز أحدا إلا بعد معرفته الوقف والابتداء

NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.speaker: الشعبي
NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says not to pause after kullu man ʿalayhā fān until reciting wa-yabqā wajhu rabbika dhu al-jalāli wa-l-ikrām.
NASHR:v1p224#2/r6.anchor: وصح عندنا عن الشعبي، وهو من أئمة التابعين علما وفقها ومقتدى أنه قال: إذا قرأت كل من عليها فان

NASHR:v1p427/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p427/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p427/r1.claim: Ibn Dhakwān's transmitted sakt may accompany either long or medium madd; the source says both combinations are transmitted.
NASHR:v1p427/r1.anchor: إذا قرئ بالسكت لابن ذكوان يجوز أن يكون مع المد الطويل ومع التوسط لورود الرواية بذلك

NASHR:v1p427/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p427/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p427/r2.claim: For Ḥafṣ, sakt requires madd and cannot accompany qaṣr: al-Ashnānī from ʿUbayd transmits sakt only with madd, while al-Fīl from ʿAmr transmits qaṣr only with idrāj.
NASHR:v1p427/r2.anchor: فإنه لا يكون إلا مع المد. ولا يجوز أن يكون مع القصر ; لأن السكت إنما ورد

NASHR:v1p427/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p427/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p427/r3.claim: For Ḥamza at a pause, easing hamza within one word cancels sakt or tahqīq; across words, rules for easing the separated hamza determine sakt or its absence.
NASHR:v1p427/r3.anchor: فإن كان الساكن والهمز في الكلمة الموقوف عليها، فإن تخفيف الهمز كما سيأتي ينسخ السكت

NASHR:v1p427/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p427/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p427/r4.claim: On al-arḍ and al-insān, Ḥamza has naql or sakt; on qad aflaḥ, man āmana, and qul ūḥiya, as well as qālū āmanna, fī anfusikum, and mā unzila, sakt, no sakt, and naql occur. Yā ayyuhā and hāʾulāʾ allow only tahqīq or easing, never sakt.
NASHR:v1p427/r4.anchor: لم يتأت له في نحو (الأرض، والإنسان) سوى وجهين، وهما: النقل والسكت

NASHR:v1p427/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p427/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p427/r5.claim: Ḥamza's madd must accompany sakt, on the definite article alone or also on separated madd. The apparent report of Khallād's madd on shayʾ without sakt is disallowed; madd there functions as sakt.
NASHR:v1p427/r5.anchor: لا يجوز مد شيء لحمزة حيث قرئ به إلا مع السكت إما على لام التعريف فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#2/r1.claim: ‘All upon it’ means those on the earth prepared for living beings, including animals and composite bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#2/r1.anchor: على الأرض التي وضعت للأنام من الحيوانات والمركبات

ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p108#2/r2.claim: The relative pronoun من either includes things with rational beings predominant or specifically denotes humans and jinn.

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r2.claim: من may include animals or material beings on earth by grammatical predominance, or both humans and jinn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:25-36/r2.anchor: من على الأرض من الحيوانات أو المركبات

BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r13.claim: Everything on earth—including both land and sea—and even the heavens will perish; all besides God is contingent, existing between nonexistence before creation and nonexistence after extinction.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r13.anchor: أي هالك ومعدوم بالفعل بعد أن كان هو وغيره من سائر ما سوى إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r14.claim: Creatures undergo continual making and unmaking in their states, qualities, and powers, while causes of destruction surround them unseen, as they do passengers in a ship.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p383/r14.anchor: ثم هو فيما بين ذلك يتعاوره الإيجاد والإفناء في حين من أحواله وأعراضه وقواه

DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī advises readers not to stop after the statement that all on earth perish, but to continue through the statement that God's face remains.
DURR-FULL:v7p698/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} فلا تسكت حتى تقرأ {ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r1.claim: عليها refers to the earth by context, just as the phrase about the sun disappearing behind a screen uses a pronoun without naming the sun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r1.anchor: وضمير { عليها } مراد به الأرض بقرينة المقام مثل { حتى توارت بالحجاب } ( ص : 32 ) ، أي الشمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r2.claim: فان means destined to perish; the active participle refers to future time, as in the statement that both you and they will die.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r2.anchor: ومعنى { فان } : أنه صائر إلى الفناء ، فهذا من استعمال اسم الفاعل لزمان الاستقبال بالقرينة مثل { إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r3.claim: Those upon the earth are humans, the intended subjects of this lesson; من is used because it refers specifically to rational beings.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.claim: Everyone on earth will perish; the reminder of death points beyond it to the reckoning and recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p252/r4.anchor: والمعنى : أن مصير جميع من على الأرض إلى الفناء ، وهذا تذكير بالموت وما بعده من الجزاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114/r1.claim: Those upon the earth will perish; the expression refers by metonymy to the earth, which is not expressly named, and fānin means doomed to perish.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p114/r1.anchor: أي على الأرض وهي كناية عن غير المذكور فان أي هالك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r1.claim: All inhabitants of earth will die, as will the inhabitants of the heavens except whom God wills; only God's noble Face remains, because the Lord is ever-living and never dies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r1.anchor: أن جميع أهل الأرض سيذهبون ويموتون أجمعون، وكذلك أهل السموات، إلا من شاء الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.claim: Qatada says God first informed people about what He created, then informed them that all of it would pass away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: أنبأ بما خلق، ثم أنبأ أن ذلك كله كان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.speaker: الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says one should not stop after reciting that all on earth perish, but continue through the declaration that God's Face remains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p494/r4.anchor: وقال الشعبي: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} ، فلا تسكت حتى تقرأ

MUQATIL:55:24-28/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r4.claim: Every living creature on earth will perish.
MUQATIL:55:24-28/r4.anchor: { كل من عليها فان } [آية: 26] يعني من على الأرض من الحيوان، فإنه يعني هالك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p202#2/r1.claim: “All who are upon it” means everyone on earth, who will perish.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r1.claim: The pronoun upon it refers to earth, mentioned at the beginning of the surah; Arabic may refer to earth even without explicit prior mention.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r1.anchor: للأرض، وقد جرى ذكرها في أول السورة

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the angels thought earth’s inhabitants had perished when this verse came down; after 28:88 was revealed they became certain of death.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة هلك أهل الأرض فنزلت:

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r3.claim: One blessing in creatures’ passing is that death makes all people equal.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r3.anchor: في الموت، ومع الموت تستوي الأقدام.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r4.claim: Another blessing is that death transfers people to the abode of recompense and reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:26-27/r4.anchor: وقيل: وجه النعمة أن الموت سبب النقل إلى دار الجزاء والثواب.

QASHANI:55:19-27/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:19-27/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:19-27/r8.claim: All aboard the sailing vessels reach God through annihilation in Him.
QASHANI:55:19-27/r8.anchor: كل من على الجواري السائرة واصل إلى الحق بالفناء فيه

QASHANI:55:19-27/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:19-27/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:19-27/r9.claim: Alternatively, every particular being on the body’s earth—spirit, intellect, heart, soul, their stations and ranks—vanishes on reaching the goal.
QASHANI:55:19-27/r9.anchor: كل من على أرض الجسد من الأعيان المفصلة كالروح والعقل والقلب والنفس ومنازلها ومقاماتها ومراتبها

RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in عليها refers to the earth, understood though not named; Razi supports the omission with Qur'anic usage such as 35:45.

RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r2.claim: After mentioning ships at sea in 55:24, Razi says people know their bodies, souls, and wealth are in God's grasp there, but forget this on solid ground; earth's heavy sinking in water is even more astonishing than the light heavens floating.
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى أن كل أحد يعرف ويجزم

RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r3.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun to refer to the ships: everyone aboard is close to perishing and cannot control benefit or harm; 55:27 supports the preferred earth reading.

RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r4.claim: Although all things on earth perish, the verse singles out rational beings because they are the ones who benefit from the warning.
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r4.anchor: المنتفع بالتخويف هو العاقل فخصه تعالى بالذكر

RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r5.claim: To answer why people are called perishing if they will perish only later, Razi compares the future sense with 39:30, where the living Prophet is called dead, and with calling something near already arrived.

RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, human existence is an accident and so does not persist; worldly existence alternates between origination and nonexistence, with no lasting continuation.

RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r7.claim: This does not entail the claim that bodies fail to last for two moments: man denotes a body with transient accidents, so the whole does not remain unchanged even though the body remains; that body alone is not literally man.
RAZI-FULL:v29p92#2/r7.anchor: ومن مع كونه على الأرض يتناول جسما قام به أعراض

RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r1.claim: The reminder that everything on earth perishes urges people to spend their brief time in worship and obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r1.anchor: الحث على العبادة وصرف الزمان اليسير إلى الطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r2.claim: It prevents the prosperous from trusting that their wealth and possessions will last and neglecting to turn back to God.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r2.anchor: المنع من الوثوق بما يكون للمرء

RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r3.claim: It teaches those in distress to be patient rather than disbelieve on the assumption that hardship will soon pass.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r3.anchor: الأمر بالصبر إن كان في ضر فلا يكفر بالله معتمدا على أن الأمر ذاهب والضر زائل

RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r4.claim: It forbids worshipping others and warns against relying on closeness to kings instead of seeking nearness to God, since rulers and their worldly order soon disappear.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r4.anchor: ترك اتخاذ الغير معبودا والزجر على الاغترار بالقرب من الملوك وترك التقرب إلى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r5.claim: A courtier who dies before his king meets God like a runaway slave; one left after the king dies faces revenge and shame, and if both die, their meeting with God is very difficult.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r5.anchor: لأنه إن مات قبلهم يلقى الله كالعبد الآبق

RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r6.claim: The verse supports true monotheism and abandoning both open and hidden idolatry, because what perishes is not fit to be worshipped.
RAZI-FULL:v29p93/r6.anchor: حسن التوحيد وترك الشرك الظاهر والخفي جميعا لأن الفاني لا يصلح لأن يعبد

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.claim: The passage recalls 28:88, where all things perish except God’s Face.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r1.anchor: Cf. 28:88: All things perish, save His Face

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.claim: These verses turn the sūrah from earthly blessings in vv. 10–25 to the blessings of the Hereafter in the remaining verses.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r2.anchor: These verses mark an important turn in this sūrah, as vv. 10–25 refer to the blessings or boons of this world

STUDYQURAN:55:26/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r3.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r3.claim: Most take “what is upon it” as the earth, its face, or this world generally, meaning all creation will pass away.
STUDYQURAN:55:26/r3.anchor: It is taken by most as a reference to the earth, the face of the earth, or this world in general

TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.claim: All jinn and humans on the earth will perish, while God's face remains, possessing majesty and honor.
TAB-FULL:v22p212/r1.anchor: الجلال والإكرام؛ وذو الجلال والإكرام من نعت الوجه فلذلك رفع ذو

SULAMI:v2p294#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r1.claim: Junayd says whoever stands between the two ends of annihilation is perishing.
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r1.anchor: سئل الجنيد رحمة الله عليه عن قوله : ﴿ كل من عليها فان ﴾ فقال : من كان بين طرفي فناء فهو فان .

SULAMI:v2p294#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says whoever persists in following desire is perishing without realizing it.
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من كان مقيما على اتباع هواه فهو فان هالك من حيث لا يشعر .

SULAMI:v2p294#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r3.claim: Some define the knowledge of annihilation and abiding as knowing the world's passing and the afterlife's permanence.
SULAMI:v2p294#2/r3.anchor: سئل بعضهم عن علم الفناء والبقاء قال : هو علم فناء الدنيا وزوالها وبقاء الآخرة ودوامها

TABATABAI:55:22-27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r5.claim: The pronoun refers to the earth; every sentient, reasoning being upon it will perish, encompassing humans and jinn.
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r5.anchor: أي كل ذي شعور وعقل على الأرض سيفنى وفيه تسجيل الزوال

TABATABAI:55:22-27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r6.claim: The wording uses the rational relative pronoun for those on earth because the discourse counts God’s favors to humans and jinn in both lives.
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r6.anchor: الكلام مسرود في السورة لتعداد نعمه وآلائه تعالى للثقلين

TABATABAI:55:22-27/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r7.claim: The future sense of perishing signals the end of earthly life and the onset of the next life for its inhabitants.
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r7.anchor: في الاستقبال كما يستفاد أيضا من السياق يعطي أن قوله

TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.claim: Perishing and the advent of the life of recompense are favors, since worldly life is a preliminary stage for the afterlife; this answers the objection that perishing cannot be a favor.
TABATABAI:55:22-27/r8.anchor: وكلاهما أعني فناء من عليها وطلوع نشأة الجزاء عليهم من النعم والآلاء

TABATABAI:55:27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:27/r1.claim: Perishing means returning to God by departing this world, as many verses explain; it is not absolute annihilation.
TABATABAI:55:27/r1.anchor: حقيقة هذا الفناء الرجوع إلى الله بالانتقال من الدنيا كما تفسره آيات كثيرة

TABRISI:55:24-29/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:24-29/r5.claim: Every living creature on earth perishes and passes out of existence.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r5.anchor: كل من على الأرض من حيوان فهو هالك يفنون ويخرجون

TABRISI:55:24-29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:24-29/r6.claim: Earth is understood though not previously named, as in the Medinan expression “between its two lava tracts.”
TABRISI:55:24-29/r6.anchor: كنى عن الأرض وإن لم يجر لها ذكر كقول أهل المدينة

TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.claim: Death is a favor because it equalizes creatures, leads to reward, warns that worldly life ends, and gives moral agency: immediate reward would compel action and erase its merit.
TABRISI:55:24-29/r12.anchor: النعمة فيه التسوية بين الخلق فيه وأيضا فإنه وصلة إلى الثواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r1.claim: ʿAlayhā refers to the earth mentioned earlier at 55:10; every creature that moves across the earth will perish.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r1.anchor: أي على الأرض، وقد سبق ذكرها في قوله {والأرض وضعها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.claim: They report that the angels concluded the people of earth had perished when this verse was revealed, then became certain of their own destruction when 28:88 was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: لما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة: هلك أهل الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.speaker: الشعبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says a reader should not pause after the statement that all on earth perish, but continue into the statement that the Lord's face remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p158/r3.anchor: قال الشعبي: إذا قرأت {كل من عليها فان} فلا تسكت حتى تقول: {ويبقى وجه ربك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r6.claim: Every living creature on earth will perish.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:19-29/r6.anchor: كل من عليها } على الأرض من حيوان { فان } هالك.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.claim: After enumerating worldly blessings, the passage reminds readers that they and their inhabitants are finite while absolute permanence belongs only to God; lasting happiness calls for a life pleasing to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:26/r1.anchor: bütün bunların geçici ve üzerinde yaşayanların sonlu olduğu, mutlak anlamda kalıcılığın ise Allah Teâlâ’ya mahsus bulunduğu hatırlatılarak

BURHAN:v2p51/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p51/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p51/r6.claim: The permanence of the Lord’s face does not conflict with the statement that all on earth perish.

ITQAN:v3p180/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p180/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p180/r3.claim: The warning that all on earth perish is itself a blessing: it moves people from a troubled abode to joy and relieves the righteous believer from the wicked.
ITQAN:v3p180/r3.anchor: فأجيب بأجوبة أحسنها النقل من دار الهموم إلى دار السرور وإراحة المؤمن والبار من الفاجر

ITQAN:v1p222/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p222/r1.speaker: الشعبي
ITQAN:v1p222/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says not to pause after 55:26 but to continue reading through 55:27; Suyuti says Ibn Abi Hatim recorded this.
ITQAN:v1p222/r1.anchor: وصح عن الشعبي أنه قال إذا قرأت ﴿ كل من عليها فان ﴾ فلا تسكت حتى تقرأ ﴿ ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام ﴾

ITQAN:v3p236/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p236/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p236/r1.claim: Iftinān joins two modes, praise and consolation: God comforts all creatures capable of life by announcing their end, then praises His own abiding majesty and generosity in ten words.
ITQAN:v3p236/r1.anchor: هو الإتيان في كلام بفنين مختلفين كالجمع بين الفخر والتعزية في قوله تعالى ﴿ كل من عليها فان ويبقى وجه ربك ذو الجلال والإكرام ﴾

ITQAN:v3p236/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p236/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p236/r2.claim: The phrase ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا joins gladness with consolation as another instance of the figure.
ITQAN:v3p236/r2.anchor: ﴿ ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ﴾ الآية جمع فيها بين هناء وعزاء

BURSEVI:v9p243/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p243/r4.claim: In 'all upon it perishes,' the pronoun refers to earth even though earth was not explicitly mentioned, as in an Arabic idiom that likewise uses an unstated antecedent.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r4.anchor: الهاء كناية عن غير مذكور كقولهم إذا نهى السفيه جرى إليه

BURSEVI:v9p243/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p243/r5.claim: The author reads 'all' as all earthly animals and composite beings, or as the two accountable peoples, humans and jinn; min is used generically in either reading.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r5.anchor: والمعنى كل من على الأرض من الحيوانات والمركبات ومن للتغليب على الوجهين أو من الثقلين

BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.speaker: الملائكة
BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.claim: The angels first thought the children of Adam had perished when this verse was revealed; after 'every soul tastes death' was revealed, they realized they too would die, since their subtle bodies and attached spirits perish, though the lofty, immaterial spirits do not.
BURSEVI:v9p243/r6.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية قالت الملائكة : هلكت بنوا آدم

BURSEVI:v9p244/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p244/r6.claim: 'All upon it perishes' signifies either natural death, submerged in sensual and bodily pleasures, or voluntary death, shedding human traits and taking on spiritual qualities.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r6.anchor: إما بالموت الطبيعي منغمسا في بحر الشهوات الحيوانية واللذات الجسمانية وإما بالموت الإرادي منسلخا عن الصفات البشرية

BURSEVI:v9p244/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p244/r7.claim: The predominance implied by min points to people of sound intellect, free from the defects of imagination; they pass away from natural conditions and abide through divine manifestations.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى ذوي العقول السليمة عن آفات

BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.claim: Some say that deeper discernment reveals the actual perishing of the universe even while it appears to exist, since what depends on another is not truly self-subsisting; real existence belongs to the pre-eternal.
BURSEVI:v9p244/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لو نظرت بنظر التحقيق في الكون وأهله لرأيت حقيقة فنائه وفناء أهله

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in “upon it” refers to the earth, either by proximity or directly to the earlier mention of Earth.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r1.anchor: Bu عَلَيْهَا zamiri cevârî dolayısıyla yahut doğrudan doğru yukarıdaki “Arz”a râci‘dir.

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r2.claim: Everyone on earth perishes, including those aboard ships as well as everyone else.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r2.anchor: Yani o Arz üzerinde bulunan her kim olursa olsun hepsi fânîdir. Gerek o gemilerdekiler, gerek diğerleri hepsi de

BURHAN:v4p411/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p411/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p411/r7.claim: The relative man can be modified by either a single word or a clause; one reading of كل من عليها فان means every person established upon it.
BURHAN:v4p411/r7.anchor: ثم الموصولة قد توصف بالمفرد وبالجملة

BURHAN:v4p176/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p176/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p176/r3.claim: The verse says ‘upon it’ rather than ‘in the earth’ because, at annihilation, there is no state of settled permanence or establishment.
BURHAN:v4p176/r3.anchor: لأن عند الفناء ليس هناك حال القرار والتمكين

BURHAN:v4p26/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p26/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p26/r10.claim: Context allows an omitted earth in phrases about creatures on its back or everyone upon it; Ibn Mālik instead takes the pronoun as the world, inferred from a previously mentioned part.
BURHAN:v4p26/r10.anchor: وجعل ابن مالك الضمير للدنيا وقال وان لم يقدم لها ذكر لكن تقدم ذكر بعضها والبعض يدل على الكل

ITQAN:v2p547#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r7.claim: Context can supply an omitted antecedent that the listener understands: the earth or world, and the deceased in the inheritance phrase, though not previously named.
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r7.anchor: وقد يدل عليه السياق فيضمر ثقة بفهم السامع نحو ﴿ كل من عليها فان ﴾ ﴿ ما ترك على ظهرها ﴾ أي الأرض أو الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r7.claim: Every animal living on earth will perish.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p445#2/r7.anchor: {كل من عليها} أي على الأرض من حيوان فإنه هالك {فان}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.claim: From the statement that all on earth perish through this passage are admonitions, restraints, and warnings; they are blessings because they deter sin, which is why each verse ends by asking which favors are denied.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p450#3/r1.anchor: وكل ما ذكر الله تعالى من قوله: "كل من عليها فان" إلى ههنا مواعظ وزواجر وتخويف. وكل ذلك نعمة من الله تعالى، لأنها تزجر عن المعاصي ولذلك ختم كل آية بقوله: {فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r2.claim: This refrain is not a tailpiece to the statement that all on Earth perish, and perishing itself is not a favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p254/r2.anchor: تكرير كما تقدم وهذا الموقع ينادي على أن ليست هذه الجملة تذييلا لجملة { كل من عليها فان } ( الرحمن : 26 )

BURHAN:v3p19/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p19/r1.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v3p19/r1.claim: An unnamed commentator counts the Rahman sequence as seven worldly blessings, seven warnings, a central verse of shared mortality, then two groups of eight verses describing the gardens, totaling thirty-one.
BURHAN:v3p19/r1.anchor: وقال غيره نبه في سبع منها على ما خلقه الله للعباد من نعم الدنيا المختلفة على عدة أمهات النعم
